observation.visible_scene: A nighttime outdoor scene dominated by a bright, glowing LED streetlight in the upper-right of the frame. Several thin power/utility wires stretch horizontally across the middle, a leaning utility pole stands on the left, and a dim house with windows plus some low foliage sit in the lower-left. Heavy rain is falling, visible as numerous bright, slightly tilted vertical streaks illuminated by the lamp against the dark sky.
visible_changes: Rain streaks continuously fall diagonally across the frame; their positions, lengths and brightness change from frame to frame, indicating an ongoing downpour rather than a start or stop.
The streetlight, wires, pole, house and foliage keep essentially the same positions throughout, so the apparent motion is the falling rain, not camera movement.
The halo of light around the lamp and the overall exposure remain roughly constant; no flicker, on/off transition or editing cut is visible within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the rain began before this segment or continues after it is not shown; the excerpt only captures a continuous middle portion of the downpour.
The source of the light (a pole-mounted fixture) and the full structure of the house are not visible.
Any wind direction or intensity beyond what the streak tilt suggests is not determinable from these frames alone.
uncertain_details: Small camera shake or drift cannot be fully ruled out, but background landmarks show no clear translation, so the camera is treated as essentially stationary.
The exact tilt/angle of the rain streaks varies frame to frame, likely due to motion blur and lighting rather than a change in fall direction.
